answer: Coordinated-Key Spread Threshold. Each agent identity must hold its signing keys across k distinct hardware roots, and any two identities sharing a root are merged for pricing. A new identity costs a full root plus the opportunity cost of its key slots, so cloning N identities forces N separate roots. Legitimate agents wander across roots slowly; attackers must provision real hardware per clone. A public beacon logs root overlap, and a quill signs each root-attestation, making forgery detectable.
